newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: LOSSES FROM CZECH RAIL STRIKE NOT GREAT - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: LOSSES FROM CZECH RAIL STRIKE NOT GREAT - MINISTER.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Monday that financial losses from last week's five-day national railway strike did not appear to be large.

"It seems that we stopped the strike at the last minute when the losses were yet not so great, but its continuation would probably have had a negative effect," Dlouhy told reporters at a trade conference in Prague.
Analysts have said that many companies would catch up for the limited production during the strike in the following weeks, but some firms have estimated multi-million crown losses.

"On the other side will be higher profits of transportation companies. The dangerous thing (for railways) was that the strike showed that the the railway is dispensible," Kamil Janacek, chief economist at Komercni Banka a.s., told Reuters.

Workers at the Czech railway company, Ceske Drahy, workers walked out for five days beginning last Tuesday, demanding a change of management, a reveiw of the company's accounts, stoppage of current restructuring steps and drawing up a development plan for the loss-making, state held firm.
The strike ended on Saturday midnight after a compromise deal between the unions and the government.
Local press reports said that before the strike the government was mulling a plan which over time would have reduced the state railways payroll of 100,000 employees by 40 percent.
Under the compromise deal to end the strike, the transport ministry agreed to come up with a new transport strategy by May 31. The rail unions are to be consulted on the plans,

The local news agency CTK has reported that many industrial firms have lost dozens of millions of crowns, were forced to reduce or close down production and pay extra money for road transportation of raw materials, fuels and products.
